{"self_assessment": "Impact: I got the table's design onto the pad quickly. I sketched the fish as two smooth, rounded lines leaving from the nose, with the tail lobes at the ends. That gave everyone one shared plan and a shape a single push could run through, with no sharp corners. By the end, our check showed 107 of the 108 standing dominoes connected to the start, and the outline reads as a fish with a forked tail.

Execution: I traced the whole bottom line (stroke 2) from the nose out toward the tail. I stood back up the pale, unconnected dominoes on the top line and pulled out the extras sitting under it. I inspected the run closely twice before the push, and my final check confirmed the chain ran from the nose to both tail lobes.

Collaboration: I kept the table informed throughout, giving clear updates on what I was laying and where the line ended. I handed the tail end of the bottom line to Tom at a clean stopping point and accepted Leo's offer to take the far end by the tail. I also told people to keep a hand's width apart near the nose to avoid bumps. In the last minutes I called for hands off so nothing was disturbed before the push.

Leadership: I took the initiative on the plan by sketching it myself, assigned the strokes so every line had an owner, and set up the handoffs at the tail. I called the final readiness check and kept the table calm for the push. The result was a team effort, but I believe the shared sketch and the bottom line were central to it.", "my_share_percent": 35}
